description: Arrived in El Salvador in the late 1960s with Aerolíneas El Salvador (AESA) as YS-032C; formally bought by the Fuerza Aérea Salvadoreña in December 1976 as FAS 301 and used mainly as a freighter to the USA and Panama. Last reported flight 1991; grounded by an incomplete fuel-tank repair. On static display on the museum's south ramp since 2004. Reconditioned internally in March 2013 into a computer classroom for schools near the air base; repainted; and at that time wrongly renumbered FAS 302; it now again carries its correct FAS 301. Flotilla Aérea criticises both the classroom conversion and the arbitrary renumbering as inconsistent with museum practice.

Built 1944. Served with the Brazilian Air Force as FAB-2036 before being handed to the FAS by the US Government on 23 December 1984 in AC-47 gunship configuration. Withdrawn after a landing accident at Ilopango. Only the cockpit section survives; displayed inside the museum building since 2001.

Built as an HC-123B and converted to C-123K in 1968. In Vietnam it was General William Westmoreland's personal transport; named "White Whale". Pulled from MASDC storage and delivered to the FAS on 29 March 1984; ten years of Salvadoran service; retired 1994. On display at the south-west side of the museum building since 2004.

Ex-Israeli Ouragan; airframe series 430; delivered to the FAS on 24 August 1974. Withdrawn after a landing accident on Ilopango runway 33 in the early 1980s. Displayed at the entrance to the San Jacinto cable car between roughly 1982 and 1983 as the replacement for the FG-1D Corsair that had stood there; and while there it wore the FALSE tail number 007. Vandalism and neglect at that site caused its return to the FAS. Only the cockpit section is displayed; inside the museum building; since 2001.

Four-seat post-war fabric-covered single; airframe serial 1626; still fitted with its original 150 hp Franklin 6A4-335-B3 engine. Owned by Sr. Francisco Escobar Thompson and donated to the museum; displayed in the central gallery since close to the museum's opening in December 2001. Photo credit Tim Spearman.
Delivered to the FAS in September 1987. Withdrawn from use and the fuselage sectioned; only the cabin section is displayed; inside the museum building.
aliases: UH1D; UH-1D; Huey; Iroquois; c/n 5888; 66-16194; UH1

description: First flew 22 January 1979; a 727-225/AF freighter flown by Eastern Air Lines; HCL Aviation; Atlantic Island Air and; from 1993; Federal Express; where it carried the name "Ray". Made its final landing at Ilopango (MSSS) on 29 June 2013. Now serves as a ground-instruction airframe for the Universidad Don Bosco and is parked on the west side of the museum building. Borderline record: it is retained and publicly visible at a museum but its primary current function is technical training; not interpretation.
